idea: Energy transition risk research for generalist funds
buyer: Generalist PMs holding industrials, utilities and materials
pain: Transition exposure is material and generalists cannot assess it
v1: A quarterly transition-risk note on ten held names
channel: Her fund network, informed by father's policy contacts
verdict: Where her father's network and her own job description genuinely meet; strongest tailwind in the set.

why.distribution: 20-50 warm generalist PMs - exactly her peer group - plus credibility from her father's policy access.
why.demand: Funds buy thematic research; transition exposure is a live board-level question, though untested at this price.
why.fmf: Generalist coverage plus genuine energy-policy access is a combination very few independents hold.
why.revenue_structure: Contracted monthly or annual subscription that renews once it enters a fund's process.
why.defensibility: Policy access via her father is genuinely hard to replicate; the analysis itself is not.
why.leverage: One note serves every subscriber; occasional bespoke questions are the only per-client cost.
why.time_to_revenue: A first pilot subscriber from her network within 1-3 months.
why.tailwind: Energy-transition mandates and disclosure obligations both carry budget and are still tightening.

ceiling_arithmetic: £1,200/mo x 15 funds = £216k gross, less ~£10k data = £206k net - clears the bar if contracts are annual and billed upfront. Monthly billing halves year-one cash to ~£120k.
carries: Two of her assets at once, a genuinely budgeted tailwind, subscription economics, and only 15 clients needed.
kills: Nothing structural. The risk is that generalist funds treat transition risk as an ESG checkbox rather than a research purchase.
test: Offer three generalist PMs a free transition note on names they hold, then quote £1,200/mo.
test_pass: One asks for a contract or takes it to a budget holder.
test_fail: They say their ESG team or data vendor covers it.
